newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady at 3.05/3.10 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady at 3.05/3.10 percent.

text.p: German call money rates were steady at 3.05/3.10 percent on Tuesday as commercial banks' deposits at the Bundesbank remained below requirements, dealers said.
Dealers said the bulk of deals were conducted at 3.08 percent but one dealer noted that demand had eased somewhat from Monday.
Looking ahead to Wednesday's tender, dealers said they expected a net funds injection of up to two billion marks. A 67.8 billion marks facility at a fixed rate of three percent expires tomorrow.

Dealers said the market was unmoved by comments by Bundesbank deputy president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum, who said in a newspaper interview that the Bundesbank might soon move to scrap reserve requirements on repo business.

Bank desposits with the central bank rose to 36.5 billion marks on Monday from 35.9 billion while the monthly average remained at 27.2 billion marks. Borrowings at the Lombard window were an unchanged 100 million marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= on Tuesday was at 3.10867 versus 3.10400.
